cell_type_model: human monocyte-derived dendritic cells and activated human T cells; Lgals1-null and wild-type mouse immune models
assay_or_perturbation: Galectin-1 affinity capture, surface-plasmon-resonance and CD69-Fc binding; recombinant Gal-1 treatment; CD69 blockade and Th17 differentiation assays
relation_type: Direct glycan-dependent LGALS1-CD69 binding is required for a Gal-1-mediated suppressive T-cell differentiation output; no unique CD69 cytosolic relay was resolved
pathway_branch: LGALS1-CD69 inhibitory immune-regulation branch -> suppression of Th17 differentiation
limitations: The primary study establishes direct carbohydrate-dependent binding and CD69-dependent immune function, but CD69 lacks a defined signaling sequence in this assay and the downstream molecular relay is unresolved. Gal-1 also binds other glycoprotein receptors in T-cell contexts; no terminal TF occupancy was measured.

cell_type_model: human vascular smooth-muscle cells and cell-surface integrin preparations
assay_or_perturbation: 125I-Gal-1 chemical cross-linking and beta1-integrin immunoprecipitation; beta1-integrin activation and FAK-associated tyrosine-phosphorylation readouts; beta-galactoside controls
relation_type: LGALS1 binds the ITGB1-containing integrin receptor and induces outside-in integrin activation with cytoskeletal/FAK signaling and adhesion effects
pathway_branch: LGALS1-ITGB1-containing integrin -> integrin activation -> FAK/cytoskeletal adhesion branch
limitations: The assay identifies the beta1 subunit and does not define the alpha partner or a purified heterodimeric affinity. FAK phosphorylation and adhesion are receptor-proximal/cellular outputs; no terminal TF endpoint was measured.

cell_type_model: recombinant human soluble endoglin and galectin-3; CHO-K1 transfectants; human endothelial-cell membrane glycoproteins
assay_or_perturbation: Protein microarray, biolayer interferometry, co-immunoprecipitation and co-localization; galectin-3 affinity purification from endothelial-cell membranes
relation_type: Direct LGALS3-ENG glycoprotein association
pathway_branch: LGALS3-endoglin glycan-dependent endothelial receptor-complex branch
limitations: Direct interaction is supported by recombinant and cell-based assays, but the endothelial affinity-purification study identified multiple glycoproteins and did not isolate an ENG-specific signaling output. Endoglin/TGF-beta pathway evidence was not transferred to a direct LGALS3-ENG relay; no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: human HUVEC and HMEC-1 endothelial cells; recombinant CD146/MCAM ectodomain
assay_or_perturbation: Galectin-3 affinity purification, glycan-dependent co-localization, pull-down, gel filtration and biolayer interferometry; CD146 knockdown; AKT, cytokine-secretion and endothelial-migration assays
relation_type: LGALS3 binds N-glycosylated MCAM/CD146, promotes receptor dimerization and activates an AKT-linked endothelial functional output
pathway_branch: LGALS3-MCAM/CD146 -> receptor dimerization -> AKT -> endothelial cytokine secretion/migration
limitations: The interaction is glycan-dependent and cell-context dependent; galectin-3 also binds other endothelial glycoproteins. AKT and cytokine/migration responses are measured outputs, not evidence of a universal MCAM-specific transcriptional endpoint.

cell_type_model: recombinant human Mac-2-binding protein; human 293 kidney cells; A549 and H1299 lung-adenocarcinoma cells
assay_or_perturbation: M2BP solid-phase and cell-adhesion assays with beta1-integrin blocking antibodies; co-localization/co-immunoprecipitation, ITGB1 silencing, adhesion/invasion assays and TGF-beta/SMAD2 readouts
relation_type: LGALS3BP is an extracellular cell-adhesion ligand for an ITGB1-containing integrin context and supports an ITGB1-dependent TGF-beta functional axis
pathway_branch: LGALS3BP-ITGB1-containing integrin -> adhesion/TGF-beta-SMAD2 EMT branch
limitations: The foundational study supports beta1-dependent adhesion but does not specify the alpha partner or purified receptor affinity. The recent LUAD study adds co-localization/co-IP and ITGB1-silencing evidence in a tumor model; SMAD2 is a pathway readout, not a validated terminal TF endpoint for the exact pair.

cell_type_model: mouse brain membrane preparations, transfected HEK293T/COS7 cells and mouse hippocampal synaptic models
assay_or_perturbation: ADAM22 immunoprecipitation/mass spectrometry, quantitative cell-ELISA and surface-binding assays; Lgi1-null and rescue experiments; synaptic-complex and AMPA-receptor transmission readouts
relation_type: LGI1 directly binds ADAM22 and organizes an ADAM22-linked synaptic receptor/scaffold complex that regulates excitatory transmission
pathway_branch: LGI1-ADAM22 -> PDZ/MAGUK-Kv1/AMPA synaptic complex -> excitatory transmission
limitations: ADAM22 is a non-catalytic adhesion/receptor component and the downstream effect is a multicomponent synaptic-complex output rather than a canonical kinase cascade. The submitted pair is exact, but the functional phenotype depends on associated ADAM23, MAGUK and ion-channel components; no terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: mouse brain membrane and hippocampal synaptic complexes; transfected mammalian cells; human LGI1-mutant receptor assays
assay_or_perturbation: Quantitative cell-surface ELISA, co-immunoprecipitation and synaptic-complex analysis; LGI1 loss/rescue and secretion-positive epilepsy-mutant binding assays
relation_type: Direct LGI1-ADAM23 binding within an LGI1-ADAM22/ADAM23 trans-synaptic complex
pathway_branch: LGI1-ADAM23/ADAM22 synaptic adhesion complex -> Kv1/AMPA organization
limitations: The molecular interaction is directly supported, but the cited functional phenotypes are properties of the linked ADAM22/ADAM23 complex and do not isolate an ADAM23-only intracellular relay. ADAM23 has no established cytosolic signaling sequence in these assays; no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: mouse neuronal growth-cone models; COS7 cells expressing NgR1/RTN4R and ADAM22; human variant-binding assays
assay_or_perturbation: Recombinant LGI1 binding to NgR1, cell-spreading/growth-cone assays, NgR1-ADAM22 complex analysis and LGI1/RTN4R variant perturbations
relation_type: LGI1 binds RTN4R/NgR1 in an ADAM22-associated receptor complex and antagonizes myelin-induced growth inhibition
pathway_branch: LGI1-RTN4R/NgR1-ADAM22 -> myelin-inhibition antagonism -> neurite outgrowth/growth-cone branch
limitations: RTN4R is GPI-anchored and requires co-receptors, especially ADAM22, for full signaling context. The studies establish binding and receptor-dependent cellular function but do not define a unique RTN4R intracellular relay or terminal TF.

cell_type_model: mouse myelinated peripheral and central axons; primary neuronal/oligodendrocyte models; Lgi2/Lgi3 and Adam23 mutant mice
assay_or_perturbation: LGI2/3 localization and loss-of-function genetics, ADAM23-dependent juxtaparanodal Kv1 clustering, electrophysiology and recombinant protein interaction/comparator assays
relation_type: LGI2 associates with ADAM23-containing juxtaparanodal complexes and contributes redundantly with LGI3 to ADAM23-dependent Kv1-channel organization
pathway_branch: LGI2-ADAM23 -> juxtaparanodal Kv1 complex clustering -> axonal refractory-period control
limitations: The study identifies LGI2 as a partially redundant ADAM23 ligand in vivo, with LGI3 the major ligand; the exact LGI2-ADAM23 biochemical contribution is not isolated as a standalone affinity measurement. This is a neuronal receptor-complex/function edge, not a conventional kinase relay; no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: mouse oligodendrocytes and myelinated axons; primary neuronal cultures; Lgi3-null and Adam23-null mice
assay_or_perturbation: LGI3 secretion/localization, ADAM23-dependent juxtaparanodal accumulation, mutant-mouse genetics, electrophysiology and recombinant ADAM23/LGI-complex assays
relation_type: LGI3 is an extracellular ADAM23 ligand that organizes ADAM23/Kv1 juxtaparanodal complexes and supports short-term axonal electrical function
pathway_branch: LGI3-ADAM23 -> ADAM23/Kv1 clustering -> axonal refractory-period and short-term plasticity branch
limitations: The primary study establishes a strong receptor-complex/function relationship but does not resolve a cytosolic ADAM23 kinase/adaptor sequence. LGI2 is partially redundant, and the observed phenotype is specific to myelinated axonal compartments; no terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: mouse Schwann-cell/sensory-neuron co-cultures, developing peripheral nerves and enteric glial progenitors
assay_or_perturbation: ADAM22-Fc pull-down and cell-surface binding; cell-type-specific Lgi4 or Adam22 deletion; heterotypic cultures, myelination and gliogenesis assays
relation_type: LGI4 binds the ADAM22 ectodomain directly and drives receptor-dependent peripheral glial differentiation and myelination
pathway_branch: LGI4-ADAM22 -> axon-Schwann/glial receptor-complex branch -> PNS myelination and gliogenesis
limitations: The exact direct interaction and receptor dependence are strong, but ADAM22 is non-catalytic and the intracellular relay connecting the complex to Schwann-cell differentiation remains unresolved. Effects are developmental and PNS-specific; no terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: transfected mammalian cells, developing mouse PNS, and curated human LGI-ADAM complex records
assay_or_perturbation: LGI4 co-immunoprecipitation and cell-surface binding to ADAM23; comparative ADAM11/22/23 binding and LGI4 developmental-function studies
relation_type: Direct LGI4-ADAM23 receptor-complex association
pathway_branch: LGI4-ADAM23 neuronal adhesion and ADAM-family receptor-complex branch
limitations: Primary assays support binding of LGI4 to ADAM23, but the functional myelination/gliogenesis phenotype is specifically strongest for ADAM22 and does not establish an ADAM23-specific intracellular relay. Reactome is retained as a pathway-context cross-check only; no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: HEK293/HeLa cells expressing LHCGR; recombinant LH alpha/beta hormone and LHCGR mutant systems
assay_or_perturbation: BRET ligand-receptor proximity using eGFP-tagged LHB/CGA and Gluc-LHCGR; recombinant LH stimulation, cAMP and calcium assays; receptor-mutant binding/function controls
relation_type: The LHB subunit contributes to the intact LH alpha/beta glycoprotein ligand that binds and activates LHCGR through Gs/cAMP and Ca2+-linked outputs
pathway_branch: LHB/CGA intact LH -> LHCGR -> Gs/adenylyl cyclase/cAMP and Gq/11-Ca2+ branch
limitations: LHB was tested as part of the intact alpha/beta hormone or an LHB-CGA fusion, not as an independently active isolated beta subunit. LHCGR signaling is pleiotropic and the cited assay does not establish a terminal TF.

cell_type_model: rat neonatal cardiac myocytes and mouse/human LIFR-gp130 receptor-complex systems; M1-UR21 myeloid cells
assay_or_perturbation: LIF stimulation, gp130/LIFR receptor-complex mutants and blocking antibody, gp130/JAK1/STAT3 phosphorylation, MAPK activation, differentiation and in vivo cardiac stimulation
relation_type: LIF activates the assembled LIFR-IL6ST/gp130 receptor complex with receptor-proximal JAK/STAT3 and MAPK outputs
pathway_branch: LIF-LIFR-IL6ST/gp130 -> JAK1/STAT3 and ERK/MAPK -> differentiation/cardiac response branch
limitations: The submitted receptor label is a composite complex rather than a binary IL6ST-only or LIFR-only edge. LIF receptor stoichiometry and tissue-specific branch use vary by model; STAT3 phosphorylation is measured, but a universal STAT3-exclusive transcriptional program was not established.

cell_type_model: rat kidney proximal tubules; recombinant RAP/LRP2 megalin systems
assay_or_perturbation: RAP gene disruption, RAP affinity chromatography, megalin processing/localization and renal protein-reabsorption assays; recombinant megalin/RAP structural and binding analyses
relation_type: LRPAP1/RAP binds LRP2/megalin as an ER/Golgi chaperone and ligand-binding regulator
pathway_branch: LRPAP1-RAP -> LRP2/megalin maturation and endocytic handling branch
limitations: This is an intracellular receptor-chaperone association, not an extracellular ligand-triggered signaling event. RAP deficiency changes megalin processing and uptake, but no LRP2 kinase relay or terminal TF endpoint was demonstrated.

cell_type_model: cultured hippocampal neurons, COS7/HEK cell-adhesion systems and recombinant LRRC4B/NGL-3 with LAR/PTPRF ectodomains
assay_or_perturbation: Recombinant ectodomain binding/domain mapping, cell aggregation and trans-synaptic co-culture synaptogenesis assays
relation_type: LRRC4B/NGL-3 directly binds the extracellular FNIII domains of PTPRF/LAR and induces presynaptic differentiation in a trans-synaptic adhesion complex
pathway_branch: LRRC4B-NGL3/PTPRF-LAR -> trans-synaptic adhesion and receptor-PTP organization -> excitatory synapse formation
limitations: The exact interaction is supported, but the output is an adhesion-organizer function rather than a defined PTPRF substrate or kinase cascade. LAR-family splice and synaptic context matter; no terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: activated lymphocyte LTalpha1beta2 ligand systems; HeLa/293T NF-kappaB reporter cells; mouse embryo fibroblasts
assay_or_perturbation: LTalpha1beta2-LTBR binding stoichiometry and structural analysis, site-directed receptor-binding mutants, LTBR-dependent NF-kappaB reporter assays and LTBR pathway perturbation
relation_type: Membrane LTalpha1beta2 heterotrimer binds and dimerizes LTBR, triggering receptor-proximal TRAF/NIK/IKK signaling and canonical/non-canonical NF-kappaB activity
pathway_branch: LTA1B2-LTBR -> TRAF/NIK/IKKalpha-beta -> canonical and non-canonical NF-kappaB branch
limitations: The ligand is the membrane-anchored heterotrimer, not isolated LTA or LTB. LTBR signaling includes time-dependent RelA and RelB complexes and other outputs; the exact ligand-receptor structure study used engineered ligand variants and NF-kappaB reporters rather than a tissue-specific SCI model, so no terminal TF is assigned here.

cell_type_model: rat primary osteoblasts, human SaOS-2 osteoblasts and LRP1-null/wild-type fibroblasts
assay_or_perturbation: Lactoferrin binding and receptor-associated protein blockade, LRP1 antibody inhibition, LRP1-null rescue/comparator assays, p42/44 MAPK and mitogenesis readouts
relation_type: LTF binds an LRP1-containing receptor context and drives receptor-dependent endocytic and mitogenic MAPK signaling in osteoblast models
pathway_branch: LTF-LRP1 -> LRP-family endocytic/signaling branch -> ERK1/2 MAPK -> osteoblast proliferation
limitations: The primary study reports LRP1/LRP2 expression and RAP-sensitive lactoferrin responses, with the strongest signaling assignment to LRP1 in LRP2-negative SaOS-2 and LRP1-null comparisons. LRP1 is a multiligand receptor and no terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: rabbit growth-plate/resting/articular chondrocytes, human epiphyseal chondrocytes and MRC5 fibroblasts
assay_or_perturbation: Matrilin-1/CMP-coated adhesion substrates, integrin-blocking antibodies, cell spreading and alpha1 co-immunoprecipitation of radiolabeled CMP
relation_type: MATN1/CMP associates with ITGA1 in an alpha1beta1 integrin context and promotes chondrocyte/fibroblast adhesion and spreading
pathway_branch: MATN1-alpha1beta1 ECM adhesion and cartilage-remodeling branch
limitations: The primary result identifies the alpha1 subunit and shows beta1-dependent blockade, but it does not isolate a purified MATN1-alpha1beta1 affinity or intracellular relay. The output is adhesion/spreading; no terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: rabbit and human chondrocytes/fibroblasts on cartilage-matrix substrates
assay_or_perturbation: Matrilin-1-coated adhesion/spreading assays with beta1-integrin blockade and alpha-subunit comparison; radiolabeled CMP co-immunoprecipitation
relation_type: MATN1-mediated cell adhesion requires an ITGB1-containing alpha1beta1 integrin receptor, but the beta1-only label does not specify the complete receptor
pathway_branch: MATN1-ITGB1-containing alpha1beta1 -> cartilage-cell adhesion and spreading
limitations: ITGB1 is a shared integrin subunit and the exact alpha partner is alpha1 in this study; no beta1-only direct molecular interface or intracellular pathway was resolved. No terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: human SW-13 cells, WI-38 fibroblasts, HUVEC, neuroblastoma and glioblastoma cells
assay_or_perturbation: MDK binding to ALK-expressing cells, ALK ligand-domain antibody blockade, ALK phosphorylation, PI3K/MAPK activation, soft-agar colony formation and endothelial proliferation assays
relation_type: MDK binds and activates ALK in receptor-expressing cells, inducing receptor phosphorylation and PI3K/MAPK growth and survival outputs
pathway_branch: MDK-ALK -> ALK phosphorylation -> PI3K/ERK-MAPK -> growth, survival and angiogenic outputs
limitations: The primary study supports cell-based MDK-ALK binding and ALK-dependent signaling, but later literature notes that MDK receptor composition can include LRP/integrin/PTPZ complexes and that the high-affinity direct interface remains debated. No terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: mouse N2a neuroblastoma cells and recombinant/epitope-tagged glypican-2 systems
assay_or_perturbation: MK-coated microbeads/substrata, glypican-2 clustering and cell-surface ligation; antibody and transfection assays; adhesion and neurite-outgrowth readouts
relation_type: Direct heparan-sulfate-dependent MDK-GPC2 binding promotes GPC2 clustering, neuronal adhesion and neurite outgrowth
pathway_branch: MDK-GPC2 proteoglycan clustering -> neuronal adhesion and neurite-outgrowth branch
limitations: GPC2 is a glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchored proteoglycan without a defined cytosolic signaling domain; the study does not establish a unique intracellular relay or terminal TF. Heparan-sulfate-chain dependence limits interpretation as a conventional binary protein interface.

cell_type_model: mouse L cells with wild-type or LRP-deficient backgrounds; human and mouse MDK receptor comparator systems
assay_or_perturbation: 125I-MDK binding/internalization, LRP expression or rescue, nuclear translocation, nucleolin-binding and mutant-nucleolin perturbation; cell-survival readouts
relation_type: MDK binds an LRP1/LRP-containing endocytic receptor context that mediates internalization and nucleolin-dependent nuclear targeting
pathway_branch: MDK-LRP1 -> endocytosis -> nucleolin-assisted nuclear targeting -> cell-survival output
limitations: The original study used an LRP preparation and LRP-deficient/rescue cells rather than an LRP1-purified receptor, so exact LRP1 identity and stoichiometry remain context dependent. This is an endocytic/nuclear-targeting branch, not a demonstrated LRP1 kinase relay; no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: mouse L cells, PYS-2 and 3T3 cells; human/mouse cell-surface and nuclear-targeting systems
assay_or_perturbation: Nucleolin affinity purification/ligand blotting, MDK-binding-site mapping, nuclear-localization-signal mutant nucleolin and MDK internalization/survival assays
relation_type: MDK directly associates with cell-surface/intracellular nucleolin after LRP-dependent uptake and uses NCL as a nucleocytoplasmic shuttle
pathway_branch: MDK-NCL -> nucleocytoplasmic shuttling/nuclear targeting -> MDK survival and growth output
limitations: NCL is multifunctional and the source studies distinguish cell-surface/nucleocytoplasmic nucleolin from a canonical transmembrane receptor. NCL-dependent nuclear targeting is established, but no direct transcription-factor occupancy or canonical kinase relay was measured.

cell_type_model: human HaCaT keratinocytes and pancreatic-cancer cell models; recombinant MDK/Notch2 systems
assay_or_perturbation: MDK stimulation and knockdown, Notch2 ectodomain binding, NICD2 nuclear accumulation, JAK2/STAT3 pathway readouts, EMT and chemoresistance assays
relation_type: MDK binds NOTCH2 and activates a NOTCH2-NICD/JAK2-STAT3 functional branch
pathway_branch: MDK-NOTCH2 -> NICD2 nuclear transmission/JAK2 -> STAT3 -> EMT and chemoresistance
limitations: The primary keratinocyte and cancer studies support a context-specific MDK-NOTCH2 association and pathway output, while the receptor-complex mechanism is not fully resolved and may involve additional MDK receptors. STAT3 is recorded because it is directly measured in the cited MDK-NOTCH2 pathway; no claim is made that it is the sole endpoint.
